name: Fucked Up
label: Matador
lede: A Toronto hardcore band with a name no newspaper would print won Canada's top music prize with flutes, French horns and a screamer called Pink Eyes, then wrote a 77-minute rock opera and a twenty-year cycle of songs named after the Chinese zodiac.

eras.title: Aliases, sigils and seven-inches
eras.text: Fucked Up started in Toronto in 2001 as a hardcore band that hid behind stage names (10,000 Marbles, Concentration Camp, Mustard Gas, Pink Eyes) and put out a blizzard of limited singles. From the start the records looked like occult pamphlets and the songs kept getting longer.

years.h: Fucked Up forms in Toronto under fake names
years.p: [[Mike Haliechuk|06275171-c023-495b-98d7-fac7671fed48]] (10,000 Marbles), [[Josh Zucker|16ca8eac-3b25-45d0-8535-c1c46d5cf08d]] (Concentration Camp), Sandy Miranda (Mustard Gas) and drummer [[Chris Colohan|f1494c0a-331d-45dd-a51c-6c43d43ccc69]] start the band; [[Damian Abraham|a718a47a-e63c-4c59-8b98-5df130e57f64]], Pink Eyes, joins before the demo.
years.xp: Zucker started on vocals before moving to guitar once Abraham came in. [[Jonah Falco|62eca584-0333-4bbd-be97-b71d04cc230f]], Mr. Jo, replaced Colohan on drums, and Colohan went on to front Cursed.

years.h: No Pasaran, the first 7-inch
years.p: Fucked Up's first single, No Pasaran, is followed within a year by The Police (March 2003) and Baiting the Public (May 2003).

years.h: Epics in Minutes gathers the early singles
years.p: A CD compilation rounds up Fucked Up's singles, the same year the band self-released the Looking for Gold 12-inch in runs of 300 and 400 copies.

eras.title: The Hidden World and the zodiac
eras.text: The debut album ran 72 minutes, longer than most hardcore bands' whole careers, and the band launched a series of long singles named for the Chinese zodiac that would take twenty years to finish. On Canadian TV, their shows started wrecking studios.

years.h: Year of the Dog starts the Zodiac series
years.p: The Year of the Dog 12-inch launches Fucked Up's Zodiac series: one long piece per sign of the Chinese zodiac.

years.h: Hidden World: 72 minutes of hardcore
years.p: Jade Tree releases Fucked Up's debut on CD and Deranged puts it out as a double LP. Exclaim! names it the No. 1 punk album of the year.
years.xp: [[Owen Pallett|6d394418-a565-4c16-9dec-f5a89e213cde]], then recording as Final Fantasy, plays violin. Guest vocalists include [[Alexisonfire|bc1c8f3f-6f36-4086-a470-87ed813dd429]]'s George Pettit and [[Dallas Green|06b65c62-b894-45ec-88f4-b7d689851e35]], Chris Colohan, and Ben Cook of No Warning, a year before he joined.

q: Damian Abraham, on the washroom show
years.h: MTV Canada bans moshing after Fucked Up's set
years.p: Introduced as 'Effed Up' on MTV Live in Toronto, the band plays Baiting the Public while the crowd does about $2,000 in damage and cuts Damian Abraham's forehead. MTV Canada bans moshing.
years.xp: They came back on October 9, 2008, and played in the MTV Live men's washroom. Band and fans tore out the ceiling, spray-painted the walls and knocked over amps and a prop motorcycle; the show was stopped after one song. MTV hadn't known the destruction was planned.

years.h: Ben Cook of No Warning joins on guitar
years.p: Ben Cook, who sang on Hidden World as a guest, joins Fucked Up as rhythm guitarist and backing vocalist.

years.h: David Christmas, with Nelly Furtado and David Cross
years.p: Fucked Up's holiday single David Christmas features [[Nelly Furtado|13655113-cd16-4b43-9dca-cadbbf26ee05]], [[Davey Havok|0d7bf43a-d747-4c8b-bc4c-927d9a7fe03a]], David Cross, Shenae Grimes and Faris Badwan.

years.h: The New York Times prints them as asterisks
years.p: Fucked Up are filmed in New York for Richard Roepnack's film Burn. The New York Times reviews it kindly but prints the band's name as asterisks.

eras.title: Flutes, a lawsuit and the Polaris Prize
eras.text: The second album brought in French horns, flutes and orchestral players, and a hardcore band was suddenly on critics' lists everywhere. Fucked Up sued Rolling Stone, played for twelve hours on the Bowery, and beat Canada's indie establishment for the Polaris Prize.

years.h: Fucked Up and Xiu Xiu sue Rolling Stone and Camel
years.p: Fucked Up and [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]] sue Rolling Stone and Camel cigarettes over an Indie Rock Universe ad they say made them look like cigarette supporters.
years.xp: A California appeals court threw out the suit on January 28, 2010, on free speech and press grounds.

years.h: Keith Morris sings Circle Jerks songs with them in Austin
years.p: At Austin's Mess With Texas fest, [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] of the [[Circle Jerks|22995eba-1238-4b4f-a937-ac2c5767ab9f]] sings Backed Against the Wall, Beverly Hills and Black Flag's Nervous Breakdown with Fucked Up.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Chemistry of Common Life
years.h: The Chemistry of Common Life on Matador
years.p: Recorded in Toronto with producer Jon Drew, Fucked Up's Matador debut is 52 minutes of hardcore with flute, French horn and organ. Pitchfork gives it 8.8.
years.xp: The title comes from a book by James F. W. Johnston about the hallucinogenic properties of mushrooms and plants, and the cover shows Manhattanhenge. Members of [[Vivian Girls|d0676301-7ffc-4ff6-8b38-f8aeb8553115]] and Dallas Green sing on it.

years.h: A 12-hour show in New York with Moby and Dinosaur Jr.
years.p: To mark the album, Fucked Up play for twelve hours on the Bowery. Guests include [[Ezra Koenig|6900fc31-d624-422c-9aa8-b3e6c8cc25ea]], [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], [[John Joseph|64581915-b050-4a79-b1bf-29fdf6005093]] of the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]], Les Savy Fav and [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]

years.h: The Festival of the Fuck Bands, in Fucking, Austria
years.p: Fucked Up play with [[Holy Fuck|4342cf80-7c06-4402-a431-457e77310474]], Fuck and [[Fuck Buttons|f4640b20-b76b-40d3-9ffc-a38b6718b273]] in the Austrian village of Fucking.

years.h: Jello Biafra and Keith Morris at the Echoplex
years.p: At the Echoplex in Los Angeles, [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] joins Fucked Up for the Ramones' Blitzkrieg Bop, and Keith Morris repeats his Circle Jerks cameo.

years.h: Damian Abraham turns down a job at Fox News
years.p: Damian Abraham declines Fox News' offer to be a regular left-wing guest on Red Eye; host Greg Gutfeld had named The Chemistry of Common Life the best album of 2008.

years.h: The Chemistry of Common Life wins the Polaris Prize
years.p: A screaming hardcore record wins the 2009 Polaris Music Prize for the best Canadian album of the year.

years.h: A Do They Know It's Christmas? cover for a cause
years.p: Fucked Up's all-star cover, with [[Ezra Koenig|6900fc31-d624-422c-9aa8-b3e6c8cc25ea]], [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]] members, Kevin Drew, [[Tegan and Sara|d13f0f47-36f9-4661-87fe-2de56f45c649]], [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] and GZA, raises money for groups working on Canada's missing and murdered Indigenous women.

eras.title: A rock opera and a band growing up
eras.text: Fucked Up spent 2011 on its biggest swing: a 77-minute rock opera set in Thatcher-era England that Spin called the album of the year. Then they paused, came back for Metallica, and made a record about staying true to punk as they got older.

years.h: David's Town, a fake compilation for Record Store Day
years.p: The Record Store Day LP David's Town pretends to document bands from Byrdesdale Spa, the made-up late-1970s English town of the next album. [[A.C. Newman|bb40af12-0dfd-4a53-bfe1-666a9e49dfb2]] and [[Danko Jones|ab4721e4-bc37-4bd2-be8c-8f1550152ad6]] sing on it.

q: Really we're talking about my breaking with my girlfriend.
years.h: David Comes to Life, an 18-song rock opera
years.p: Factory worker David Eliade falls for activist Veronica Boisson, and it ends with a bombing gone wrong. Spin names the album the best of 2011.
years.xp:
The story is told by unreliable narrators, with the villain Octavio St. Laurent controlling the tale until Vivian Benson reveals what really happened. Damian Abraham said the characters let the band hide personal things, including a breakup.

It reached No. 83 on the Billboard 200 and was shortlisted for the 2012 Polaris Prize, which went to [[Feist|a670e05a-cea8-4b37-bce9-d82daf1a0fa4]].

years.h: Damian Abraham hosts The Wedge on MuchMusic
years.p: Abraham starts a three-year run hosting MuchMusic's alternative video show The Wedge (2011–2014).

years.h: Jingle Bells on Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations
years.p: Fucked Up play Jingle Bells on the Christmas episode of Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations.

years.h: Back from a break for Metallica's festival
years.p: After a hiatus from late 2011 while Damian Abraham spent time with his family, Fucked Up return at [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]]'s Orion Music + More festival in Atlantic City.

years.h: Glass Boys, about growing old in punk
years.p: Fucked Up's last Matador album, recorded partly at Electrical Audio in Chicago, has [[Gord Downie|291eb640-aa58-45e9-a8cb-069d58644b2b]] on The Art of Patrons and [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] on Led by Hand.

years.h: Damian Abraham launches Turned Out a Punk
years.p: Abraham's podcast Turned Out a Punk starts, with musicians and fans telling the story of how they found punk.

eras.title: David returns, and Ben Cook leaves
eras.text: After a four-year wait, the longest in their history, Fucked Up moved to Merge with an 82-minute double album that brought back the character David. The Zodiac cycle kept turning, and in 2021 the six-piece became five.

years.h: Zanzibar, a score for a 1928 silent film
years.p: Fucked Up self-release Zanzibar, recorded in 2011 as a soundtrack for Tod Browning's 1928 film West of Zanzibar.

years.h: Dose Your Dreams, 82 minutes on Merge
years.p: Produced by Mike Haliechuk and Jonah Falco, the double album brings back David. It's Ben Cook's last album with the band and earns a Juno nomination.

years.h: Year of the Horse, a full album for the zodiac
years.p: The ninth Zodiac installment, Year of the Horse, arrives as a whole album, self-released.

years.h: Ben Cook leaves after fourteen years
years.p: Guitarist and singer Ben Cook leaves Fucked Up. Robin Hatch fills his spot on tour.

eras.title: Twenty-four hours at a time
eras.text: Fucked Up gave themselves a new rule: each member gets one day to write and record their part. It produced a run of records, one of them written, recorded and released live on the internet, then gone after a day.

years.h: One Day: each member gets 24 hours
years.p: Mike Haliechuk wrote and recorded his guitar parts in one December 2019 session, and the others followed the same rule. The pandemic held the mix until 2022.

years.cap: Who's Got the Time & a Half?, live on the internet
years.h: An album written, recorded and released in 24 hours
years.p: Fucked Up livestream the making of Who's Got the Time & a Half? over August 6–7, 2024, then put it on Bandcamp for just 24 hours.

years.h: Another Day, the sequel to One Day
years.p: Another Day follows the same 24-hour rules, each song matching one on One Day. Someday is surprise-released November 1.

years.h: Dave Nardi joins on guitar
years.p: Dave Nardi joins as rhythm guitarist, making Fucked Up a six-piece again.

years.h: Grass Can Move Stones: the Zodiac finale
years.p: Fucked Up announce the end of the Zodiac series begun in 2006: Grass Can Move Stones, three LPs covering the Goat, the Monkey and the Rooster.
